doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Early synthesizers, Star Wars space noises and the Mini Moog
summary: Levin got into synthesizers in the early 70s and did jingle sessions making space effects on a small Moog; he still owns the Mini Moog and other vintage gear.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: got interested in synthesizers in the early 70s and for some reason I had an affinity for that and nobody else could figure them out, which was great for me. So I was doing a lot of session work. When “Star Wars” came out I was just playing as a sideman on a lot of jingles, radio and TV commercials. And there was a period where I was just going from studio to studio all week with a small Moog synthesizer and my job would be to do laser shots or space ship fly bys — sheew — that was it. 56 dollars please. Thank you. With residuals.
That’s funny. Do you still get “Star Wars” residuals?
No this could be, it was just a style. It could be a toilet paper commercial but —
Like a flushing sound or something?
It was hip to have space noises going on because “Star Wars” was really big.

It was a Mini Moog, which I still have. Actually I’ve sold very few of my instruments. Some I gave away. Some — a lot of them are vintage and are still sitting in my garage. I’m not sure how much use they are. I can’t think of what to do with them and I can’t imagine how much value — they have value to some people I’m told.
I guess people buy — I don’t know what they do with them when they buy them, they’re really limited. They’re fun to have.
